key_insight: A transfer-learning and hybrid Cross-Entropy–Lovász training strategy makes BiSeNetV2 much more robust to reflective weld seams without increasing model size or speed.
engineering_relevance: This offers a lightweight, real-time seam-segmentation upgrade for construction welding robots operating under harsh lighting and metallic glare.
method: Fine-tune a BiSeNetV2 backbone with transfer learning rather than adding architectural complexity.
Use a hybrid Cross-Entropy + Lovász loss to improve boundary quality and training stability.
Evaluate robustness on challenging reflective seam cases and compare against OHEM, DeepLabV3+, UNet, and SegFormer.
evidence_signal: The method reached 81.76% Joint IoU and 90.73% mIoU, improving Joint IoU by 22.36 points over the OHEM baseline while keeping FLOPs, parameters, and inference speed unchanged.
watch_item: Results are promising for reflective construction welds, but deployment still depends on how well the training data covers site-specific lighting, metal surfaces, and seam geometries.
paper_title: Enhanced Seam Segmentation for Automated Welding Robot in Construction Through Transfer Learning: Addressing Limitations of Bilateral Segmentation Network
